answer: Each identity binds one thoroughbred in the stud book: microchipped, DNA-matched to its pedigree, stabled at one yard; dawn gallops logged. One horse backs exactly one identity; a second claim is rejected, and weight vests after a 180-day season, win or lose. The kernel: one real horse per fake, 2,640 units all-in, so 100 fakes cost 264,000 units and 18,000 horse-days. The cheapest cheat is buying into another owner's horse, but the seller surrenders the horse backing their own identity; a forged pedigree fails the DNA check, and at its nadir a horse still needs feed, stabling and racing.
